title: Zeno ‘proved’ that the fastest runner can never catch a tortoise
body: Zeno of Elea, in the 5th century BC, argued that if a tortoise has a head start, Achilles must first reach where it was, by which time it has moved on, and so on forever. He wanted to support his teacher Parmenides’ view that change is an illusion. Calculus shows that infinitely many shrinking steps can add up to a finite time, though philosophers still debate whether that fully dissolves the puzzle.
